correctness.rationale: For every n>=3 and k, conditional-on-full-star decomposition gives k(N-k) fair mutually independent cross-edge cycle indicators. Pairwise independence of distinct other-vertex triangle indicators, and their zero covariance with each star triangle, yields the exact conditional variance. Conditioning only on score preserves both moment formulas. Centered regression and exchangeability prove the arbitrary-additive-score covariance; a binomial generating-function identity proves the Krawtchouk orthogonality. Square-criterion and both signs follow arithmetically. An independently written exact-rational enumeration of all tournaments with n=3,4,5,6 reproduced means, variances and frequency covariances; finite checks do not substitute for the proof.

originality.rationale: In the full material inspected, random-tournament score-sequence results concern convex order/realizability, local-counting work concerns quasi-randomness, and recent circular-triad work concerns asymptotic heterogeneous tournaments and classical unconditional moments. None of these statements implies the exact conditional variance given one score together with the all-additive-score degree-two projection and arithmetic zero-score classification. Separate semantic searches of published research records and the accessible prior private findings did not return a dominating theorem. The classical score-sum identity and unconditional moments are acknowledged as prior facts. Residual priority risk from inaccessible foundational literature and equivalent-statistic treatments remains.

value.rationale: Circular triads are an established paired-comparison intransitivity statistic, and win-score histograms are natural summaries. The theorem provides a finite-sample score-conditional fluctuation law, proves that among all additive score diagnostics only one orthogonal binomial mode carries linear dependence on intransitivity, and completely classifies covariance signs and exact square-order zeros. This is structural information relevant to diagnostic design and score-based assessment, not merely a single sample-size calculation. The classical deterministic score identity and unconditional moments are not represented as discoveries.
